headline: Reference-light methods advance microbial taxonomic profiling and genome-based typing
label: Computational Microbial Omics Methods
summary: Recent preprints apply ANI, breadth statistics and learned models to microbial genomes and metagenomes at database scale.
synthesis: The common thread is improving the accuracy of microbial genome and metagenome inference through explicit thresholds, benchmarking, and corrective preprocessing. Winnow-tax pairs candidate nomination with genome breadth and a Lander-Waterman breadth ratio to profile low-coverage organisms in shotgun metagenomes. genomeRxiv and BoNTax both rely on ANI-based classification: genomeRxiv provides LIN codes spanning genus to near-strain resolution across 350,000+ prokaryotic genomes, while BoNTax applies a 95% ANI threshold alongside MLST and AMRFinderPlus for C. botulinum Group I and C. sporogenes. A cyanobacterial study predicts nifHDK diazotrophy from protein-family presence (AUC 0.85-0.89) and proposes candidate families beyond known Nif proteins. Two upstream-processing items address artifacts: a 17-pipeline Nanopore trimming benchmark identifies Filtlong as top for SNP F1, and DeepMM splits chimeric contigs before binning to reduce reference-discordant annotations. BioMeBar contributes a harmonised 16S baseline across 8 Indian cohorts.
